reconcile.connective: The standard harmonization treats Chileab and Daniel as two names of one son, so the lists name the same person twice.

discrepancy.connective: Hans Wilhelm Hertzberg notes that in Chronicles "the name Daniel surprisingly takes the place of Chileab," with the old versions adding still further forms, treating the difference as a textual deviation rather than a settled second name.

skeptic.name: Hans Wilhelm Hertzberg
skeptic.work: I & II Samuel: A Commentary (Old Testament Library)
skeptic.attribution: Hans Wilhelm Hertzberg, I & II Samuel: A Commentary, Old Testament Library (Philadelphia: Westminster, 1964)

excerpts.excerpt_text: The latter is also called Daniel in Ch1 3:1, and therefore had probably two names.
excerpts.on_tension_rationale: Directly states the harmonizing inference for the Chileab/Daniel difference: one son with two names. Strongest single reconcile sentence; parity-capped to 1 on this discrepancy_first row.

pd_work.resource: Adam Clarke, The Holy Bible ... with a Commentary and Critical Notes, on 1 Chronicles 3:1 (1832)
pd_work.author: Adam Clarke
pd_work.note: Clarke treats this passage directly, arguing the second son "probably had two names" (Chileab in 2 Sam 3:3, Daniel in 1 Chron 3:1) and citing the Targum and Jarchi for the harmonizing tradition.
